title: Pea flowers and fruit formation
body: A student selects two young flower buds and three freshly opened flowers on one pea plant. She removes the stamens from one bud and from one open flower. She then loosely covers four of them with muslin cloth bags: the intact bud, the bud without stamens, the open flower without stamens and one intact open flower. The third open flower is left uncovered. After the pods on the uncovered flower are fully developed, she removes all the bags and records in a table whether a fruit (pod) has formed in each treatment. Pea flowers can pollinate themselves: their anthers can release pollen onto the stigma of the same flower, even before the flower fully opens.
